body:
Is it even necessary to have opengl as a port? The Wndows SDK include and library path is automatically (as far as I am aware) added to the Visual Studio directories search paths when you install it. Therefore the OpenGL headers and libraries are on the search path already.

To be more illustrative; I am developing a game and use GLFW3 which was installed via vcpkg. I have NOT installed opengl via vcpkg yet I can compile without issue.
You have got a point there. As it is in the list and did not work I added an issue.
So perhaps the resolution should in fact be to remove the opengl port?

The `opengl` port enables automatic linkage of `opengl32.lib` when using MSBuild, similar to `kernel32.lib`, `user32.lib`, etc. This makes it possible to run something like:

```
vcpkg install sdl2 opengl
```

and be able to copy-paste `SDL2` samples from online into a fresh project without modfiying the link line (they very often implicitly assume `opengl32.lib` will be linked).

For existing projects that already explicitly link `opengl32.lib`, you're absolutely right that it doesn't make any difference.
I am truly unable to find an example of the situation you are describing where they assume it is linked. Can you provide an example link and I will see if I can find a solution for this issue?
I think that this could also apply to me. Isn't there a way to get the directory from the environment?

issue.title: Install opengl fails with latest windows 10 sdk installed

repository.name: vcpkg
repository.description: C++ Library Manager for Windows, Linux, and MacOS

issue.body:
```
.\vcpkg install opengl
```
fails with the latest windows 10 sdk installed with the following error

```
CMake Error at ports/opengl/portfile.cmake:6 (message):
  Cannot find Windows 10.0.10240.0 SDK.  File does not exist: C:\Program
  Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib\10.0.10240.0\um\x64\OpenGL32.Lib
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  scripts/ports.cmake:73 (include)
```

Just replacing `10240` with `14393` fixes this issue, but I don't know if it should handle both version or only the latest...

issue.body:
- #### What does your PR fix?
  Fix a CI baseline regression for x64-windows-static-md, port osg.
  Fixes #28087, by ~no longer copying libs and headers out of the Windows SDK at all (ultimately) /~ using wrong case and by changes to mesa.

  I fail to see a *robust* benefit from the copying of SDK headers. AFAIU package opengl's ABI hash already doesn't depend on the Windows SDK, i.e. rebuilds of the port will be triggered independently of changes to the active version of the Windows SDK, picking what they will find at this time. And even just using exported artifacts on another machine should demand using a compatible (i.e. controlled) version of the SDK.

  Somewhat related, this PR moves the opengl32 lib generated by mesa to manual-link, and drops all mesa headers which are available from opengl-registry.

  Fixes  #28688

  Revise mesa dependencies.
  Installs a proper copyright file for mesa.

  Drafts of these changes were tested and discussed in https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/pull/28089.

- #### Which triplets are supported/not supported? Have you updated the [CI baseline](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/scripts/ci.baseline.txt)?
  unchanged, yes

  yes
